diagrams.title: Electron dot structures of methane, ethene, ethyne and CO<sub>2</sub>
diagrams.how_to_draw: Write the element symbols and place dots for valence electrons only: carbon 4, hydrogen 1, oxygen 6. In methane put one shared pair between C and each of four H atoms. In ethene put two shared pairs between the carbons and one pair to each of four H atoms; in ethyne three shared pairs between the carbons and one pair to each H. For CO<sub>2</sub> put two shared pairs between C and each O and two lone pairs on each oxygen. Use crosses for one element and dots for the other so the examiner can see whose electrons are shared.

diagrams.title: Structural isomers of butane and pentane
diagrams.how_to_draw: For butane draw the straight chain C–C–C–C with all ten hydrogens, and beside it a three-carbon chain with a CH<sub>3</sub> branch on the middle carbon. For pentane draw three skeletons: a five-carbon chain, a four-carbon chain with one CH<sub>3</sub> on carbon 2, and a three-carbon chain with two CH<sub>3</sub> groups on carbon 2. Check that every carbon has exactly four bonds and that the hydrogen count matches the formula.

diagrams.title: Structures of cyclohexane and benzene
diagrams.how_to_draw: Draw a regular hexagon with a carbon at each vertex. For cyclohexane attach two hydrogens to each carbon and use single bonds only (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>). For benzene attach one hydrogen to each carbon and draw alternate single and double bonds around the ring (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>). If the question mentions cyclopentane, draw a pentagon with two hydrogens on each carbon.

diagrams.title: Structures of ethanol, ethanoic acid, propanone and ethyl ethanoate
diagrams.how_to_draw: Show every bond. Ethanol: CH<sub>3</sub>–CH<sub>2</sub>–O–H. Ethanoic acid: CH<sub>3</sub>–C(=O)–O–H with the double bond to one oxygen drawn explicitly. Propanone: CH<sub>3</sub>–C(=O)–CH<sub>3</sub> with the carbonyl in the middle. Ethyl ethanoate: CH<sub>3</sub>–C(=O)–O–CH<sub>2</sub>–CH<sub>3</sub>. Label the functional group in each.

diagrams.title: Micelle and the cleaning action of soap
diagrams.how_to_draw: Draw an oil droplet as a shaded circle. Around it draw fifteen or twenty soap molecules as matchsticks: a wavy tail inside touching the oil and a round head on the outside in water. Label the hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail, the hydrophilic ionic head (–COO<sup>−</sup>Na<sup>+</sup>), the oily dirt at the centre and water outside. Add a caption saying the charged heads repel each other so micelles stay suspended and are rinsed away.

ncert_questions.q: What would be the electron dot structure of carbon dioxide which has the formula CO<sub>2</sub>?
ncert_questions.a: Carbon (2, 4) needs four electrons; each oxygen (2, 6) needs two. Carbon shares two electron pairs with each oxygen atom, giving two double bonds: O=C=O. In the dot structure, place four shared dots (two pairs) between C and each O, and two lone pairs (four dots) on the outer side of each oxygen. Every atom now has eight electrons in its outer shell.

ncert_questions.q: How many structural isomers can you draw for pentane?
ncert_questions.a: Three. (i) n-pentane: a straight chain of five carbons, CH3–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH3. (ii) A four-carbon chain with a methyl branch on the second carbon: CH3–CH(CH3)–CH2–CH3. (iii) A three-carbon chain with two methyl branches on the middle carbon: CH3–C(CH3)2–CH3. All three have the molecular formula C5H12.

ncert_questions.q: What are the two properties of carbon which lead to the huge number of carbon compounds we see around us?
ncert_questions.a: (i) Catenation: carbon atoms bond with other carbon atoms to form long chains, branched chains and rings, with single, double or triple bonds, because the C–C bond is strong. (ii) Tetravalency: each carbon atom forms four covalent bonds, with carbon or with other elements such as H, O, N, S and halogens, so a huge variety of compounds is possible. Both properties are helped by the small size of the carbon atom, which makes its bonds strong and its compounds stable.

ncert_questions.q: What will be the formula and electron dot structure of cyclopentane?
ncert_questions.a: Cyclopentane is a ring of five carbon atoms, each bonded to two hydrogens, so its formula is C5H10. Draw a pentagon with a carbon at each corner; between neighbouring carbons place one shared pair of electrons, and on each carbon place two hydrogens, each sharing one pair with the carbon. There are 5 C–C bonds and 10 C–H bonds, all single, 15 in total.

ncert_questions.q: Draw the structures for the following compounds: (i) Ethanoic acid (ii) Bromopentane (iii) Butanone (iv) Hexanal. Are structural isomers possible for bromopentane?
ncert_questions.a: (i) Ethanoic acid: CH3–COOH, i.e. a carbon with one double-bonded O and one –OH attached to CH3. (ii) Bromopentane: CH3–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2–Br (C5H11Br). (iii) Butanone: CH3–CO–CH2–CH3. (iv) Hexanal: CH3–CH2–CH2–CH2–CH2–CHO. Yes, structural isomers of bromopentane are possible: the bromine can be attached to carbon 1, 2 or 3 of the straight chain, and the chain itself can be branched with the bromine at different positions, giving several compounds of formula C5H11Br.

ncert_questions.q: How would you name the following compounds? (i) CH<sub>3</sub>–CH<sub>2</sub>–Br (ii) H–CHO (iii) a six-carbon chain with a terminal C≡C bond
ncert_questions.a: (i) Two carbons with a bromine: bromoethane. (ii) One carbon with an aldehyde group: methanal. (iii) Six carbons with a triple bond at the end of the chain: hexyne (hex-1-yne). Rule: count the longest chain for the root (eth, meth, hex), then attach the halogen as a prefix and the aldehyde or triple bond as a suffix (-al, -yne).

ncert_questions.q: Why is the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid an oxidation reaction?
ncert_questions.a: Ethanol is CH3CH2OH (C2H6O) and ethanoic acid is CH3COOH (C2H4O2). In the conversion an oxygen atom is added and two hydrogen atoms are removed. Addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen is oxidation, so the reaction is an oxidation. It is brought about by oxidising agents such as alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7: CH3CH2OH → (alk. KMnO4, heat) → CH3COOH.

ncert_questions.q: A mixture of oxygen and ethyne is burnt for welding. Can you tell why a mixture of ethyne and air is not used?
ncert_questions.a: Air is about 78% nitrogen and only about 21% oxygen, so with air the supply of oxygen is limited. Ethyne, an unsaturated hydrocarbon with a high carbon content, then burns incompletely, giving a sooty yellow flame and a low temperature, and the soot spoils the metal surface. With pure oxygen ethyne burns completely, CH≡CH burning to CO2 and H2O, and the flame is clean and extremely hot, hot enough to melt and weld metals.

ncert_questions.q: How would you distinguish experimentally between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid?
ncert_questions.a: Add a small amount of sodium carbonate (or sodium hydrogencarbonate) to each sample. The carboxylic acid reacts with brisk effervescence, releasing carbon dioxide that turns lime water milky: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2. The alcohol gives no reaction with sodium carbonate. Alternatively, a carboxylic acid turns blue litmus red while an alcohol has no effect on litmus.

ncert_questions.q: What are oxidising agents?
ncert_questions.a: Oxidising agents are substances that are capable of adding oxygen to other substances (or removing hydrogen from them). Examples are alkaline potassium permanganate (KMnO4) and acidified potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7), both of which oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid.

ncert_questions.q: Would you be able to check if water is hard by using a detergent?
ncert_questions.a: No. Detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids whose charged ends do not form insoluble salts with the Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions in hard water. A detergent therefore gives good lather in both hard and soft water, so it cannot tell the two apart. Soap can: in hard water it forms scum instead of lather.

ncert_questions.q: People use a variety of methods to wash clothes. Usually after adding the soap, they beat the clothes on a stone, or beat it with a paddle, scrub with a brush or the mixture is agitated in a washing machine. Why is agitation necessary to get clean clothes?
ncert_questions.a: Soap molecules attach to the oily dirt with their hydrophobic tails and form micelles around it, but the dirt is still held on the fibres of the cloth. Agitation (beating, scrubbing or the tumbling of a machine) supplies the mechanical force needed to loosen the dirt particles from the fibres so that the micelles carrying them can be pulled into the water and rinsed away. Without agitation much of the dirt stays trapped in the cloth.

ncert_questions.q: Ethane, with the molecular formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, has (a) 6 covalent bonds (b) 7 covalent bonds (c) 8 covalent bonds (d) 9 covalent bonds.
ncert_questions.a: (b) 7 covalent bonds. The two carbons share one C–C bond, and each carbon carries three hydrogens, giving 6 C–H bonds. Total 6 + 1 = 7.

ncert_questions.q: Butanone is a four-carbon compound with the functional group (a) carboxylic acid (b) aldehyde (c) ketone (d) alcohol.
ncert_questions.a: (c) ketone. The suffix -one denotes a ketone: butanone is CH3–CO–CH2–CH3, with the carbonyl carbon bonded to carbon atoms on both sides.

ncert_questions.q: While cooking, if the bottom of the vessel is getting blackened on the outside, it means that (a) the food is not cooked completely (b) the fuel is not burning completely (c) the fuel is wet (d) the fuel is burning completely.
ncert_questions.a: (b) the fuel is not burning completely. Incomplete combustion, usually because the burner holes are blocked and the air supply is limited, produces unburnt carbon (soot) that deposits on the vessel and gives a yellow flame.

ncert_questions.q: Explain the nature of the covalent bond using the bond formation in CH<sub>3</sub>Cl.
ncert_questions.a: Carbon (2, 4) has four valence electrons and needs four more; hydrogen (1) needs one; chlorine (2, 8, 7) needs one. In chloromethane the carbon atom shares one electron each with three hydrogen atoms, forming three C–H single bonds, and one electron with the chlorine atom, forming a C–Cl single bond. Chlorine keeps its three lone pairs. Every atom now has a complete outer shell: carbon and chlorine have eight electrons, each hydrogen has two. No electrons are transferred, so no ions form; the bonds are covalent, formed by sharing electron pairs. This is why CH3Cl is a covalent compound with a low boiling point that does not conduct electricity.

ncert_questions.q: Draw the electron dot structures for (a) ethanoic acid (b) H<sub>2</sub>S (c) propanone (d) F<sub>2</sub>.
ncert_questions.a: (a) Ethanoic acid, CH3COOH: the first carbon shares one pair with each of three H atoms and one pair with the second carbon; the second carbon shares two pairs with one oxygen (C=O) and one pair with the other oxygen, which shares one pair with H. Put two lone pairs on the C=O oxygen and two lone pairs on the O–H oxygen. (b) H2S: sulphur (2, 8, 6) shares one pair with each hydrogen and keeps two lone pairs. (c) Propanone, CH3COCH3: the middle carbon shares two pairs with oxygen (which has two lone pairs) and one pair with each CH3 carbon; each outer carbon shares one pair with each of three hydrogens. (d) F2: each fluorine (2, 7) shares one pair, F–F, and keeps three lone pairs.

ncert_questions.q: What is a homologous series? Explain with an example.
ncert_questions.a: A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds that have the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a –CH2– unit, i.e. by 14 u in molecular mass, and which can be represented by a single general formula. Example: the alkanes CH4 (methane), C2H6 (ethane), C3H8 (propane), C4H10 (butane), general formula CnH2n+2. Each differs from the previous one by CH2. Physical properties such as boiling point increase gradually along the series (methane to butane are gases, pentane onwards liquids), while chemical properties remain similar because the functional group is the same.

ncert_questions.q: How can ethanol and ethanoic acid be differentiated on the basis of their physical and chemical properties?
ncert_questions.a: Physical: ethanol is a liquid with a pleasant smell and boiling point 351 K; ethanoic acid has a pungent vinegar-like smell and melts at 290 K, freezing in cold winters (glacial acetic acid). Chemical: (i) Ethanoic acid turns blue litmus red; ethanol has no effect on litmus. (ii) Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate or sodium hydrogencarbonate with brisk effervescence of CO2 (CH3COOH + NaHCO3 → CH3COONa + H2O + CO2); ethanol gives no gas. (iii) Ethanoic acid neutralises NaOH to form sodium ethanoate; ethanol does not react with NaOH.

ncert_questions.q: Why does micelle formation take place when soap is added to water? Will a micelle be formed in other solvents such as ethanol also?
ncert_questions.a: A soap molecule has a hydrophilic ionic head (–COO−Na+) that dissolves in water and a long hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail that does not. In water the molecules arrange themselves so that the tails stay away from the water and the heads face it; the only way to do this in the bulk of the liquid is to cluster with tails pointing inward and heads outward, which is a micelle. In ethanol a micelle will not form, because the hydrocarbon tail is soluble in ethanol as well; there is no need for the tails to cluster away from the solvent.

ncert_questions.q: Why are carbon and its compounds used as fuels for most applications?
ncert_questions.a: Carbon and most of its compounds burn readily in air, releasing a large amount of heat and light; they have a high calorific value, i.e. a lot of energy per unit mass. Saturated hydrocarbons burn with a clean flame and leave no residue, since the products, carbon dioxide and water, are gases. They are also easy to store, transport and handle, and available in large amounts as coal, petroleum and natural gas. The combustion, for example CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat and light, makes them convenient fuels.

ncert_questions.q: Explain the formation of scum when hard water is treated with soap.
ncert_questions.a: Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts. Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain fatty acid. When soap is added to hard water, the Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions react with the soap anions to form the calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid, which are insoluble in water: 2C17H35COONa + Ca2+ → (C17H35COO)2Ca + 2Na+. This white, sticky precipitate is scum. It wastes soap, prevents lather from forming until all the Ca2+ and Mg2+ have been used up, and sticks to the cloth.

ncert_questions.q: What change will you observe if you test soap with litmus paper (red and blue)?
ncert_questions.a: Soap solution is basic, because soap is the salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (a fatty acid). Red litmus paper turns blue; blue litmus paper shows no change.

ncert_questions.q: What is hydrogenation? What is its industrial application?
ncert_questions.a: Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated hydrocarbon in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel or palladium to give a saturated compound: CH2=CH2 + H2 → (Ni) → CH3–CH3. Industrial application: vegetable oils, which contain long unsaturated carbon chains, are hydrogenated with nickel as catalyst to convert them into solid fats (vanaspati ghee) for cooking and food processing.

ncert_questions.q: Which of the following hydrocarbons undergo addition reactions: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>, C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> and CH<sub>4</sub>?
ncert_questions.a: C3H6 (propene, fits CnH2n, one double bond) and C2H2 (ethyne, fits CnH2n−2, one triple bond) undergo addition reactions because they are unsaturated. C2H6, C3H8 and CH4 are saturated alkanes (CnH2n+2) and do not.

ncert_questions.q: Give a test that can be used to differentiate chemically between butter and cooking oil.
ncert_questions.a: Add a few drops of bromine water to a small amount of each sample and shake. Cooking oil, which contains unsaturated fatty acid chains, decolourises the reddish-brown bromine water because bromine adds across the C=C bonds. Butter, which is largely saturated, does not decolourise bromine water. Alternatively, warm each sample with alkaline KMnO4: the oil decolourises the purple solution, butter does not.

ncert_questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the cleaning action of soaps.
ncert_questions.a: A soap molecule has a long hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail, soluble in oil, and a hydrophilic ionic head (–COO−Na+), soluble in water. Most dirt is oily and does not dissolve in water. When soap solution is applied to a dirty cloth: (i) the hydrophobic tails of soap molecules dissolve in the oily dirt while the ionic heads remain in the water; (ii) many soap molecules surround each oil droplet, forming a micelle with the dirt trapped at the centre and the charged heads on the outside; (iii) the micelles stay suspended in water as a colloid and do not coagulate because the charged surfaces repel each other; (iv) agitation loosens the micelles from the fibres and rinsing with water washes them away with the dirt. (Draw a labelled micelle around an oil droplet.)

pyq.q: Which of the following compounds will NOT undergo an addition reaction?
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> fits C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>, so it is propane, a saturated alkane with no double or triple bond, and it shows substitution, not addition. The other three are an alkene, an alkyne and an alkene.

pyq.q: Which one of the following hydrocarbons does NOT belong to the same homologous series as the others?
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>14</sub> and C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub> all fit C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> (alkanes). C<sub>7</sub>H<sub>14</sub> fits C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>, so it is an alkene (heptene) and belongs to a different series.

pyq.q: The number of single and double bonds respectively in a molecule of benzene (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>) is
pyq.answer: b
pyq.solution: Benzene has 6 C–H single bonds, 3 C–C single bonds and 3 C=C double bonds. Single bonds = 6 + 3 = 9; double bonds = 3.

pyq.q: Which of the following is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon?
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: Cyclohexane, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>, is a six-membered ring with only single bonds. Benzene and cyclohexene contain double bonds and ethyne is not cyclic.

pyq.q:
Carbon compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity and have low melting and boiling points. Which of the following statements correctly explains these properties?
(i) They have strong intermolecular forces.
(ii) They have weak intermolecular forces.
(iii) They do not form ions.
(iv) They form ions in solution.
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: Covalent compounds have weak forces between molecules, hence low melting and boiling points, and the bonding produces no ions, hence poor conductivity.

pyq.q: The functional group present in butanone is
pyq.answer: c
pyq.solution: The suffix -one indicates a ketone, whose functional group is a carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbon atoms, >C=O. Butanone is CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>.

pyq.q: Which of the following is the correct structure of a micelle formed when soap is added to water?
options: Hydrophobic tails inside, hydrophilic heads on the surface
Hydrophilic heads inside, hydrophobic tails on the surface
Both heads and tails randomly arranged
Tails dissolved in water and heads in oil
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: In water the hydrocarbon tails cluster away from water at the centre and the ionic heads face the water on the outside.

pyq.q: The first member of the alkyne homologous series is
pyq.answer: b
pyq.solution: A triple bond needs two carbon atoms, so the smallest alkyne is ethyne, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>. There is no one-carbon alkyne.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Carbon forms a very large number of compounds. Reason (R): The carbon–carbon bond is very strong, so chains and rings of carbon atoms are stable.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: The strength of the C–C bond, due to carbon's small size, allows catenation, which along with tetravalency is why carbon forms so many compounds.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Esterification is a reaction in which a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol to produce a sweet-smelling substance. Reason (R): Saponification is the reaction of an ester with a base to give an alcohol and the salt of the carboxylic acid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: b
pyq.solution: Both statements are correct on their own, but saponification does not explain why esterification produces a sweet-smelling ester; it is the reverse process.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Propanal and propanone are structural isomers. Reason (R): Both have the molecular formula C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O but different functional groups.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO (aldehyde) and CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub> (ketone) share the formula C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O and differ in structure, which is exactly what makes them structural isomers.

pyq.q: Assertion (A): Carbon forms compounds by sharing electrons rather than by gaining or losing them. Reason (R): It is energetically unfavourable for carbon to form C<sup>4+</sup> by losing four electrons or C<sup>4−</sup> by gaining four electrons.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
pyq.answer: a
pyq.solution: Removing four electrons from carbon needs too much energy and six protons cannot hold ten electrons, so carbon completes its octet by sharing; R explains A.

pyq.q: Write the names and formulae of the first two members of the homologous series of compounds containing a –Br functional group. Also name the functional groups present in CH<sub>3</sub>CHO and CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub>.
pyq.answer: First two members with a –Br group: bromomethane, CH3Br, and bromoethane, C2H5Br (they differ by –CH2–). CH3CHO contains the aldehyde group, –CHO. CH3COCH3 contains the ketone group, >C=O.

pyq.q: Write the molecular formulae of methane and propane. Why do these compounds have low melting and boiling points?
pyq.answer: Methane: CH4. Propane: C3H8. Both are covalent compounds made of discrete molecules. The forces of attraction between the molecules (intermolecular forces) are weak, so little energy is needed to separate the molecules, and the compounds melt and boil at low temperatures. (The covalent bonds within each molecule are strong, but they are not broken on melting or boiling.)

pyq.q: A saturated hydrocarbon is burnt in a good supply of air. (a) What kind of flame is observed? (b) Write the products of complete combustion.
pyq.answer: (a) A clean, blue, non-sooty flame, because a saturated hydrocarbon burns completely in sufficient air. (b) Carbon dioxide and water, with heat and light: for example CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat and light.

pyq.q: Give a chemical test to distinguish between ethane and ethene. State the observation in each case.
pyq.answer: Bromine water test. Pass each gas through (or shake it with) reddish-brown bromine water. Ethene, being unsaturated, adds bromine across its double bond and decolourises the bromine water. Ethane, being saturated, does not react and the bromine water stays reddish-brown. Alternatively, ethene burns with a sooty yellow flame while ethane burns with a clean blue flame.

pyq.q: What is denatured alcohol? Why is it made?
pyq.answer: Denatured alcohol is ethanol that has been made unfit for drinking by adding a poisonous substance such as methanol, together with a blue dye so that it can be recognised. It is made because ethanol is an important industrial solvent and is sold at low cost for industry; denaturing prevents its misuse as a drink, since even small quantities of methanol can cause blindness or death.

pyq.q: Explain, with the help of a chemical equation, why the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid is called an oxidation reaction. Name two oxidising agents used for it. How is this reaction different from the complete combustion of ethanol?
pyq.answer: CH3CH2OH → (alkaline KMnO4 + heat, or acidified K2Cr2O7 + heat) → CH3COOH. Ethanol (C2H6O) gains one oxygen atom and loses two hydrogen atoms to become ethanoic acid (C2H4O2); addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen is oxidation. Oxidising agents: alkaline potassium permanganate and acidified potassium dichromate. In complete combustion the whole molecule is oxidised to carbon dioxide and water with release of heat and light, CH3CH2OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O, whereas oxidation by KMnO4 is a controlled, partial oxidation that keeps the carbon skeleton and changes only the functional group.

pyq.q: What are isomers? Draw the structures of two isomers of butane, C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>. Explain why we cannot have isomers of the first three members of the alkane series.
pyq.answer: Isomers (structural isomers) are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements of atoms. Butane has two: (i) n-butane, CH3–CH2–CH2–CH3, a straight chain of four carbons; (ii) isobutane (2-methylpropane), CH3–CH(CH3)–CH3, a chain of three carbons with a methyl group on the middle carbon. Draw both with all hydrogens. Methane, ethane and propane cannot have isomers because one, two or three carbon atoms can be joined in only one way; a branch requires at least four carbons so that one carbon can be attached to the middle of a three-carbon chain.

pyq.q: Write the chemical equation for the reaction of ethanol with (a) sodium metal (b) excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K. Name the products and state the role of sulphuric acid in (b).
pyq.answer: (a) 2Na + 2CH3CH2OH → 2CH3CH2ONa + H2. Products: sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas (which burns with a pop). (b) CH3CH2OH → (excess conc. H2SO4, 443 K) → CH2=CH2 + H2O. Products: ethene and water. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes a molecule of water from ethanol.

pyq.q: Distinguish between addition and substitution reactions. Give one example of each with a chemical equation.
pyq.answer: Addition reaction: shown by unsaturated compounds; the double or triple bond opens and atoms add on to the carbons; two reactants give a single product. Example: hydrogenation of ethene, CH2=CH2 + H2 → (Ni catalyst) → CH3–CH3. Substitution reaction: shown by saturated compounds; one atom or group replaces a hydrogen atom; two reactants give two products. Example: chlorination of methane in sunlight, CH4 + Cl2 → (sunlight) → CH3Cl + HCl.

pyq.q: A student takes about 3 mL of ethanol in a test tube, warms it gently in a water bath and adds a 5% solution of alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub> drop by drop. (a) What is a 5% solution of KMnO<sub>4</sub>? (b) What is observed on adding the first few drops, and later on adding excess? (c) Write the chemical equation and name the role of KMnO<sub>4</sub>.
pyq.answer: (a) 5 g of KMnO4 dissolved in 95 g of water (5 g per 100 g of solution). (b) At first the purple colour of KMnO4 disappears as each drop is added, because it is used up in oxidising ethanol. Once all the ethanol has been oxidised, the purple colour of the added excess KMnO4 persists. (c) CH3CH2OH → (alkaline KMnO4, heat) → CH3COOH. Alkaline KMnO4 acts as an oxidising agent, adding oxygen to ethanol to give ethanoic acid.

pyq.q: An organic compound A of molecular formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O reacts with sodium metal to release a gas that burns with a pop. On oxidation with alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub>, A gives compound B of molecular mass 60 u. When A is heated with excess concentrated H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> at 443 K, compound C of molecular mass 28 u is formed. (a) Identify A, B and C and write their structural formulae. (b) Write the equation for the reaction of B with sodium carbonate. (c) Draw the electron dot structure of B.
pyq.answer: (a) A reacts with sodium giving hydrogen, so it contains –OH: A is ethanol, CH3CH2OH (C2H6O, 46 u). Oxidation of ethanol gives ethanoic acid, CH3COOH: mass = 2(12) + 4(1) + 2(16) = 60 u, so B is ethanoic acid. Dehydration of ethanol with hot conc. H2SO4 gives ethene, CH2=CH2: mass = 2(12) + 4(1) = 28 u, so C is ethene. Equations: 2Na + 2C2H5OH → 2C2H5ONa + H2; C2H5OH → (alk. KMnO4, heat) → CH3COOH; C2H5OH → (conc. H2SO4, 443 K) → CH2=CH2 + H2O. (b) 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2; brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide. (c) Electron dot structure of ethanoic acid: the CH3 carbon shares one pair with each of three H and one pair with the second carbon; the second carbon shares two pairs with one O (which carries two lone pairs) and one pair with the –O–H oxygen (two lone pairs), which shares one pair with H.

pyq.q: Write the chemical equations for the following reactions and name the type of reaction in each case: (a) combustion of methane (b) oxidation of ethanol by alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub> (c) reaction of ethene with hydrogen in the presence of nickel (d) reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol in the presence of concentrated H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (e) reaction of ethyl ethanoate with sodium hydroxide.
pyq.answer: (a) CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + heat and light. Combustion (complete oxidation). (b) CH3CH2OH → (alkaline KMnO4, heat) → CH3COOH. Oxidation. (c) CH2=CH2 + H2 → (Ni catalyst) → CH3–CH3. Addition reaction (hydrogenation). (d) CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH → (conc. H2SO4, warm) → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. Esterification. (e) CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH. Saponification (alkaline hydrolysis of an ester). Each part carries one mark: half for the balanced equation with conditions, half for the name.

pyq.q: Ethanol is a commercially important compound containing the –OH functional group. Write chemical equations for its reactions with (a) sodium metal (b) excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K (c) ethanoic acid in the presence of an acid catalyst (d) acidified potassium dichromate on heating. Name the main product in each case. (e) Why is ethanol mixed with petrol as a fuel?
pyq.answer: (a) 2CH3CH2OH + 2Na → 2CH3CH2ONa + H2. Product: sodium ethoxide (and hydrogen). (b) CH3CH2OH → (excess conc. H2SO4, 443 K) → CH2=CH2 + H2O. Product: ethene; the acid is a dehydrating agent. (c) CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH → (conc. H2SO4) → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. Product: ethyl ethanoate, a sweet-smelling ester. (d) CH3CH2OH → (acidified K2Cr2O7, heat) → CH3COOH. Product: ethanoic acid; K2Cr2O7 is the oxidising agent. (e) Ethanol burns completely with a clean flame giving only CO2 and water, CH3CH2OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O, and it can be made from renewable sugarcane by fermentation, so blending it with petrol gives a cleaner fuel and reduces dependence on petroleum.

pyq.q: (a) What is a homologous series? State two characteristics. (b) Write the structures of the third members of the alcohol and aldehyde series. (c) Explain with a diagram how soap cleans an oily cloth. (d) Why does soap not work well in hard water?
pyq.answer: (a) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties in which successive members differ by a –CH2– unit. Characteristics: (i) molecular masses of successive members differ by 14 u and all members fit one general formula, e.g. CnH2n+2 for alkanes; (ii) physical properties such as boiling point increase gradually with molecular mass while chemical properties stay similar. (b) Third alcohol: propanol, CH3–CH2–CH2–OH. Third aldehyde: propanal, CH3–CH2–CHO. (c) A soap molecule has a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail and a hydrophilic ionic head. In water the tails dissolve in the oily dirt and the heads stay in water; the soap molecules surround the oil droplet and form a micelle with the dirt inside. The charged heads on the surface repel one another, so the micelles stay suspended, and rinsing carries them away with the dirt. Diagram: an oil droplet surrounded by soap molecules with tails inward and heads outward, labelled. (d) Hard water contains Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions, which react with soap to form insoluble calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid (scum). Soap is used up in forming scum and gives little lather, so a lot of it is wasted.

pyq.q:
Read the passage and answer the questions. Vegetable oils generally have long unsaturated carbon chains, while animal fats have saturated carbon chains. When a vegetable oil is heated with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst, the double bonds in its chains are converted to single bonds and the oil is converted into a semi-solid fat sold as vanaspati ghee. Doctors advise the use of oils containing unsaturated fatty acids for cooking.
(i) Name the type of reaction described and write the equation for the same reaction with ethene.
(ii) What is the role of nickel in this reaction?
(iii) Give a chemical test to show that a cooking oil is unsaturated.
(iv) Why is the hydrogenated product less healthy than the original oil? OR Why does the oil become solid after hydrogenation?
pyq.answer: (i) Addition reaction, specifically hydrogenation: CH2=CH2 + H2 → (Ni) → CH3–CH3. (ii) Nickel is a catalyst: it makes the addition of hydrogen take place at a practical rate without itself being consumed. (iii) Shake a few drops of the oil with bromine water; the reddish-brown colour disappears because bromine adds across the C=C bonds. Butter or a saturated fat does not decolourise bromine water. (iv) Hydrogenation converts unsaturated fatty acid chains into saturated ones, and saturated fats are harmful for health, so the product is less healthy. OR: saturated chains pack together more closely and the intermolecular forces increase, so the melting point rises and the product is solid at room temperature.

pyq.q:
Read the passage and answer the questions. A student was given two liquids, P and Q, both with two carbon atoms. P has the molecular formula C2H6O and Q has the formula C2H4O2. Both react with sodium metal to give a gas that burns with a pop, but only Q gives brisk effervescence with sodium hydrogencarbonate. When P and Q are warmed together with a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid, a sweet-smelling liquid R is formed.
(i) Identify P, Q and R with their structural formulae.
(ii) Write the equation for the reaction of Q with sodium hydrogencarbonate.
(iii) Write the equation for the formation of R and state the role of concentrated H2SO4.
(iv) What happens when R is heated with sodium hydroxide solution? Name the reaction.
pyq.answer: (i) P is ethanol, CH3–CH2–OH (reacts with Na but not with NaHCO3). Q is ethanoic acid, CH3–COOH (reacts with both). R is the ester ethyl ethanoate, CH3–COO–CH2–CH3. (ii) CH3COOH + NaHCO3 → CH3COONa + H2O + CO2. (iii) CH3COOH + CH3CH2OH → (conc. H2SO4, warm) → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a catalyst (it also absorbs the water formed). (iv) The ester is hydrolysed back to the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH. The reaction is called saponification.

practice_mcq.q: The number of covalent bonds in a molecule of butane, C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>, is
practice_mcq.explanation: Three C–C bonds between four carbons plus ten C–H bonds gives 13.

practice_mcq.q: Which of the following belongs to the same homologous series as C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub>?
practice_mcq.explanation: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub> is an alkene (C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>); the next alkene is C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>, differing by CH<sub>2</sub>.

practice_mcq.q: Carbon does not form C<sup>4+</sup> ions because
options: removing four electrons would need a very large amount of energy
it has a large atomic size
practice_mcq.explanation: Losing four electrons to leave six protons holding only two electrons is energetically unfavourable, so carbon shares electrons instead.

practice_mcq.q: The IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO is
practice_mcq.explanation: Three carbons (prop) with an aldehyde group (–CHO, suffix -al) gives propanal.

practice_mcq.q: A compound decolourises bromine water. It must contain
practice_mcq.explanation: Bromine adds across double or triple bonds; only unsaturated compounds decolourise bromine water.

practice_mcq.q: The reaction CH<sub>4</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>Cl + HCl takes place in the presence of
practice_mcq.explanation: Substitution of hydrogen by chlorine in saturated hydrocarbons requires sunlight.

practice_mcq.q: Which of the following is used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils?
practice_mcq.explanation: Nickel (or palladium) catalyses the addition of hydrogen to the unsaturated chains of vegetable oils.

practice_mcq.q: The temperature at which ethanol is dehydrated to ethene by excess concentrated sulphuric acid is
practice_mcq.explanation: NCERT gives 443 K for the dehydration of ethanol to ethene.

practice_mcq.q: Which gas is evolved when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate?
practice_mcq.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to give salt, water and CO<sub>2</sub>, which turns lime water milky.

practice_mcq.q: The reaction of an ester with sodium hydroxide is called
practice_mcq.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester back to alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid is saponification, the process used to make soap.

practice_mcq.q: Ethanol and ethanoic acid can be distinguished by
practice_mcq.explanation: Both react with sodium and both burn, but only the acid gives effervescence of CO<sub>2</sub> with sodium carbonate.

practice_mcq.q: Pure ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid because
options: it freezes at 290 K and solidifies in cold winters
it does not mix with water
practice_mcq.explanation: Its melting point of 290 K (17 °C) means it often turns into an ice-like solid in cold climates.

options: sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids
practice_mcq.explanation: A soap such as sodium stearate is the sodium salt of a long-chain fatty acid, made by saponification of fats and oils.

practice_mcq.q: Scum forms when soap is used in hard water because
options: soap does not dissolve in hard water
Ca<sup>2+</sup> and Mg<sup>2+</sup> ions form insoluble salts with the soap anion
practice_mcq.explanation: The calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid are insoluble and separate as a sticky precipitate.

practice_mcq.q: A micelle will NOT form when soap is added to
practice_mcq.explanation: In ethanol the hydrocarbon tail of soap is soluble too, so the tails have no reason to cluster together.

practice_mcq.q: The functional group –COOH is present in
practice_mcq.explanation: The suffix -oic acid indicates the carboxylic acid group; ethanoic acid is CH<sub>3</sub>COOH.

practice_mcq.q: Which of the following has a triple bond?
practice_mcq.explanation: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>4</sub> fits C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n−2</sub>, so it is propyne with one C≡C bond.

practice_mcq.q: The number of structural isomers of pentane, C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>, is
practice_mcq.explanation: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane are the three possible arrangements.

common_mistakes: Writing only 'catenation and tetravalency' for why carbon forms so many compounds, without explaining each in a sentence and mentioning the strength of the C–C bond due to carbon's small size. The 3-mark version needs the explanation.

Saying chemical properties show gradation along a homologous series. It is the physical properties (melting point, boiling point, solubility) that change gradually; chemical properties stay similar because the functional group is the same.

Writing the oxidising agent as plain KMnO<sub>4</sub> or K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>. The examiner looks for 'alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub>' or 'acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>', with heat.

Confusing the two roles of concentrated sulphuric acid: it is a dehydrating agent in the conversion of ethanol to ethene at 443 K, and a catalyst in esterification. Swapping them costs the mark for the role.
Leaving the sodium carbonate equation unbalanced. It needs two moles of ethanoic acid: 2CH<sub>3</sub>COOH + Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> → 2CH<sub>3</sub>COONa + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub>.
Drawing isomers that are the same molecule bent differently, or drawing a carbon with five bonds. Check every carbon has exactly four bonds and re-count hydrogens after drawing.

Forgetting the condition above the arrow: sunlight for substitution, nickel catalyst for hydrogenation, 443 K with excess conc. H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> for dehydration. An equation without its condition is treated as incomplete.
Describing the cleaning action of soap without the micelle diagram, or drawing the micelle with heads inward. Tails go inward into the oil, heads face the water.
Counting the –CHO or –COOH carbon separately when naming: CH<sub>3</sub>COOH is ethanoic acid (two carbons), not methanoic acid with a methyl group.
Writing that detergents can be used to test hardness of water. They cannot; only soap fails to lather in hard water.
strategy:
This chapter is scoring because the same dozen items recur every year. Prepare in three layers. First, the ideas: why carbon forms covalent bonds (three sentences), catenation and tetravalency, saturated versus unsaturated, structural isomers of butane and pentane, and a homologous series with its four characteristics. Write each of these once from memory and check it against the section body above.

Second, the equations. There are only nine that the board asks: combustion of methane and ethanol, oxidation of ethanol, hydrogenation of ethene, chlorination of methane, ethanol with sodium, dehydration of ethanol, esterification, saponification, and ethanoic acid with NaOH, Na2CO3 and NaHCO3. Learn each with its condition written above the arrow and the name of the reaction type. Then practise the identification chain: start from C2H6O, go to ethanoic acid, ethene and ethyl ethanoate, and back to ethanol by saponification. Almost every 5-mark question is a rearrangement of this chain.

Third, the drawings: electron dot structures of CH4, CO2, ethene, ethyne and ethanoic acid; the structures of cyclohexane and benzene; and the micelle. Draw each twice on paper with labels.

Spend about two hours on the chapter in the last week: forty minutes on the ideas, forty on writing the equations from memory, twenty on drawings, and twenty on the practice MCQs and Assertion-Reason items. In the exam, for any 'identify the compound' question, write the identification with the reason first, then every equation asked, then the diagram if there is one. Marking schemes award marks per equation, so write all of them even if one looks doubtful.
